g.text: Section through one rib, square to the slope, 1:10

svg.text: Roof grid A: ruled-surface columns
one roof face seen square on
(1) Columns run in straight lines from the base edge (every 1000)
towards the crown edge, so they converge like the ruled surface of
the sketch.
(2) When the spacing drops to 500 (about +5.83) every other column
stops; at about +7.50 only the four hip columns go on to the crown
ring.
(3*) Rib (column): printed channel 160 wide x 240 deep in the 160
air zone + layer 2, filled with cast concrete, 4 Ø16 + Ø8 stirrups
every 200 (assumed).
(4) Inner layer 1, 80: continuous, covers the grid on the room
side.
(5) Outer skin 80: continuous, covers the grid on the outside
(cladding on it).
(6*) Between the ribs the air zone stays open for thermal
insulation (dotted).
* = assumed, to confirm
Notes
Columns stop on a horizontal rib (at h = 3333 and 5000
above the eave); bars are lapped / hooked into it.
Horizontal ribs at 1667, 3333, 5000, plus the 300 solid
base (bottom ring) and the top ring at the crown.
Rough quantities, four faces (hips counted twice, so
slightly high): ribs 307 m, 4 Ø16 each bars, steel 1940
kg, cast concrete 11.8 m3.
Rib size, bar count and the 160 x 240 channel are
assumptions for the engineer to check. Elevation shows the
face square on; true lengths are 1.25 x the drawn heights.
m
Scale 1:50 at A3 · dimensions in mm · draft 1, 2026-10-11
pyramid-roof · hand estimates, not engineered
